$comment: RFC-0028 — the shared verdict vocabulary. Before this file, every gating skill invented its own terminal words: feature-implement-loop says VERIFIED, pre-merge-review says READY, council-review says PROCEED, doc-critique says SHIP IT. They mean the same five things. A loop's gate declares which verdicts it can emit, and validate.py checks every one against this file — so a new loop cannot invent a sixth kind of 'yes'.

classes.pass: The gate is satisfied. The loop advances to the next stage, or terminates successfully.
classes.conditional: The gate is satisfied, but named open items travel forward with the artifact. Advancing is allowed; forgetting the items is not.
classes.revise: The gate is not satisfied and the fix is known. Return to the stage named by the loop's revision edge, subject to the cap.
classes.redirect: The gate is not satisfied and the work is the wrong shape. Do not revise — re-enter a different stage, a different loop, or a different artifact.
classes.blocked: The gate cannot be evaluated. A required input, decision, or permission is missing. Stop and name what is needed.

rules: Every gate declares at least one `pass` verdict and at least one non-pass verdict. A gate that can only succeed is not a gate.
Every gate can emit BLOCKED. A missing input is always possible and must never be fabricated past (AGENTS.md, non-interactive invocation).
A `revise` verdict is subject to the loop's `cap`. On the cap-th revise, the loop emits its conditional or blocked terminal instead of looping again.
A `redirect` verdict leaves the loop. It names where the work goes instead.
